page: Microsoft Azure DC128eds_v6 is a virtual machine instance engineered for high-concurrency enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, this server features 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. The memory subsystem is configured with 512.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The configuration lacks discrete hardware accelerators, maintaining a GPU count of zero.

A major operational differentiator of the DC128eds_v6 is its integrated local storage tier. The instance includes 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and it supports Azure Premium Storage. The combination of dense vCPU allocation, substantial system memory, and direct-attached NVMe storage allows low-latency input and output without immediate reliance on external block devices.

From an operational efficiency perspective, the DC128eds_v6 combines high compute density with bundled large-capacity NVMe disks, lowering overhead for scenarios that require large scratch spaces or persistent local caching. However, the profile excludes dedicated GPUs, limiting applicability for accelerated matrix mathematics or GPU-driven deep learning workflows.

This server type is suitable for large-scale enterprise databases, memory-intensive analytical systems, distributed data processing, and large compilation or continuous integration pipelines that demand high core counts and fast local disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure DC128eds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage capabilities include 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD space alongside support for Premium Storage. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator. Delivering massive thread concurrency and expansive local scratch space within a single host configuration, the DC128eds_v6 provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for scenarios requiring high local I/O and dense core allocation. It is best suited for large relational databases, distributed data processing, ETL pipelines, and high-capacity transactional enterprise workloads.
